To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the Regge improved spherical diquark model is able to describe a variety of phenomenological observables, including GPDs and PDFs; (ii) a Regge improved di-quark model can be constructed in terms of a few effective light-front wavefunctions, and (iii) such a model is able to predict the chiral-odd parton distribution function $h_L(x)$, the so-called Sivers function

(1) the overlap of light-front wave functions, which are obtained from the non-relativistic quark model, provides a good approximation to the double distributions that are used to model GPDs and related quantities; (2) the Regge improved quark model wave functions provide an excellent approximation to the double distribution model; (3) the Regge-improved quark model wave function provides a good description of the HERMES data for the $x$-dependent helicity distribution function

the concept of phenomenological wave functions is useful for modeling non-perturbatively the partonic structure of hadrons and for predicting the corresponding observables, that the concept of double distributions is a useful tool for modeling and predicting the partonic structure, and that the concept of Regge improved diqark model provides a useful tool for studying the role of orbital momenta.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an effective light-front theory for the description of non-perturbatively generated quark and diquark degrees of freedom in the nucleon.
the phenomenological description of the non-perturbatively generated structure of hadrons, and with the relations between different non-perturbativly generated quantities.
the phenomenological description of non-perturbatively generated parton distributions in terms of effective light-front quark and diquark wave functions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Regge improvement is a very powerful method to obtain the correct asymptotics for all the twist-two related quantities, and the correct asymptotics is the only requirement that a model has to obey.
the Regge improved di-quark model is a very useful phenomenological tool to study the parton structure of the nucleon, and to make predictions that can be compared with experimental data.
the Regge improved spherical diquark model is a viable model for GPDs, form factors, and PDFs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the concept of phenomenological wave functions is very useful in the description of parton distribution models.
a simple model for the effective light-front wave-function is sufficient to provide a good description of a wide variety of non-perturbatively calculated quantities.
we provide a unified description of the non-perturbatively calculated GPDs, form factors, and PDFs in a phenomenological model.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the phenomenological modeling of nonperturbative QCD dynamics in terms of effective light-front Hamiltonians can be extended to the description of all twist-two related quantities in the framework of a single effective light-front wavefunction.
the concept of phenomenological wave functions can be applied in a consistent way to all twist-two related quantities.

the concept of phenomenological (effective) light-front wave functions is very useful for the phenomenological description of the non-perturbatively defined quantities, including GPDs, form factors and PDFs, as well as their relations, and it is a powerful tool for a systematic study of the non-peturbative dynamics of QCD in a model-independent way.
